A car is using petrol as it travels. The graph of the amount of petrol $P(d)$, in liters, remaining in the fuel tank after traveling a distance of $d$ miles is shown above. Approximate the rate of change of the amount of petrol at $d=150$ using a forward difference with step size $h=50.$ Do not round the answer.

*Hint*: Assume that the rate of change is negative if the amount of petrol decreases.

After traveling $150$ miles, the rate of change of the amount of petrol is {{field-1}} liters per mile.

examples.problem:
An oil tank has leaked $q(t)$ liters of oil after $t$ hours. The graph of $q(t)$ is shown below. Approximate the rate at which the oil is leaking from the tank when $t=1$ using a forward difference approximation with step size $h=1.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14057748/assets/b6c5286dae7e739a588173bad9c721ae34d07f86e455e44ec9f229628cf54211.png)
examples.worked_solution:
We use the forward difference approximation

$$
q'(t) \approx \frac{q(t+h) - q(t)}{h}
$$

 

at the time $t=1$ with step size $h=1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}^{′}(1) & ≈\frac{q(1+1)-q(1)}{1} \\  & =\frac{q(2)-q(1)}{1} \\  & =3-2 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, after $1$ hour, the tank is leaking oil at a rate of approximately $1\,\textrm{liter}/ \textrm{hour}.$

feedback.problem:
The function $g(s)$ describes the amount of fuel, in liters, remaining in Samuel's car after driving $s$ miles. The values of $g(s)$ for different values of $s$ are given in the table below:

| $s$ | $0$ | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ | $10$ | $12$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $g(s)$ | $15$ | $13.5$ | $12.1$ | $9.4$ | $8.2$ | $6.6$ | $4.8$ |

Approximate the rate of change in the fuel volume when $s=8$ miles using a forward difference approximation.
feedback.worked_solution:
We use the forward difference approximation

$$
{g}^{′}(s)≈\frac{g(s+h)-f(s)}{h}
$$

 
at the point $s=8.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case $h=2.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(8) & ≈\frac{g(8+2)-g(8)}{2} \\  & =\frac{g(10)-g(8)}{2} \\  & =\frac{6.6-8.2}{2} \\  & =\frac{-1.6}{2} \\  & =-0.8.\end{aligned}
$$

So at $s=8$ the rate at which the fuel is changing is approximately $-0.8\,\text{liters/mile}.$
